ASSURANCE / MATURITY & ROADMAP

Maturity that shows its work.

Each product has a profile across assurance topics. The level records the evidence available for a stated scope; open obligations remain visible.

A catalogue label such as “Live example” or “In progress” describes delivery. It does not establish an assurance level. “Unassessed” records the absence of an assessment, without judging a product’s underlying quality.

Evidence levels

  1. Unassessed — No scoped assurance assessment is recorded.
  2. Scoped — Purpose, coverage and evidence obligations are declared.
  3. Mechanically checked — The required automated checks pass within that stated scope.
  4. Human reviewed — A dated, attributed review addresses the remaining judgment-dependent obligations.
  5. Experienced in use — Relevant people have exercised representative journeys and the findings are recorded.
  6. Maintained — Ownership, reassessment and regression evidence support continued assurance.

Identity & world coherence roadmap

Current: level 2 · Mechanically checked. Owner assignment and delivery dates remain open.

  • Next evidence gate: Semantic and visual review · level 3 · not-evidenced — Review the world assignments and discovered groups; record reviewer, method, source and date.
  • Later: Reading journeys in use · level 4 · not-evidenced — Observe readers following representative identity journeys and record the findings.
  • Later: Ongoing ownership · level 5 · not-evidenced — Assign an owner and record reassessment, regression coverage and evidence freshness.

Accessibility roadmap

Current: level 2 · Mechanically checked. Owner assignment and delivery dates remain open.

  • Next evidence gate: Human accessibility evaluation · level 3 · not-evidenced — Evaluate keyboard and focus journeys, screen-reader use, zoom/reflow and visual contrast; record findings and coverage.
  • Later: Journeys with disabled participants · level 4 · not-evidenced — Observe representative tasks with people with disabilities and record barriers and resolution.
  • Later: Accessibility maintenance · level 5 · not-evidenced — Assign ownership, review cadence and regression evidence for the assessed journeys.

Internationalisation roadmap

Current: level 1 · Scoped. Owner assignment and delivery dates remain open.

  • Next evidence gate: Locale and fallback policy · level 2 · not-evidenced — Choose target audiences, supported locales, defaults and fallback behaviour before claiming readiness.
  • Next evidence gate: Localisable content evidence · level 2 · not-evidenced — Assess message and content externalisation and supply evidence of locale selection and fallback.
  • Next evidence gate: Locale behaviour evidence · level 2 · not-evidenced — Exercise locale-sensitive numbers, dates, names, text expansion and text direction as applicable.
  • Later: Language and cultural review · level 3 · not-evidenced — Record linguistic, cultural and typographic review for each promised locale.
  • Later: Locale journeys in use · level 4 · not-evidenced — Observe representative journeys with the intended language and locale audiences.
  • Later: Localisation maintenance · level 5 · not-evidenced — Assign ownership and record translation freshness, fallback and locale regression coverage.

How a level changes

Every required gate at a level and every earlier level needs matching evidence. Missing, failed, ambiguous or differently scoped receipts block promotion. New evidence can lower a level when a required check fails. Source, issuer, method and observation date accompany each accepted receipt; those fields alone do not authenticate an evaluation.
